findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on a single raw EC2 instance with Ubuntu 12.04, Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi. No managed compute services in use. Application and database colocated.
findings.gap: No managed compute — single EC2 instance with no container orchestration, no serverless, no auto-scaling.
findings.recommendation: Containerize the application and deploy on Amazon ECS with Fargate or AWS App Runner.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 runs self-managed on the same EC2 instance as the application (localhost:5432). Backup is daily pg_dump only.
findings.gap: Database entirely self-managed with no automated failover, no managed backups, no PITR, running EOL engine.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL. No stored procedures simplifies migration.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration exists. Ticket lifecycle has no structured orchestration — all logic in imperative code paths.
findings.gap: No orchestration — all workflow logic hardcoded in application code with no visibility or retry logic.
findings.recommendation: Implement ticket lifecycle workflows using AWS Step Functions for multi-step operations.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging infrastructure. Synchronous SMTP relay to Exchange server. No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, or any messaging service.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries — email sent synchronously, no event-driven patterns.
findings.recommendation: Introduce Amazon SQS or EventBridge for state-change propagation. Use Amazon SES for email.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network security configuration in repository. No VPC, no security groups, no subnet configs. App and DB colocated on same host.
findings.gap: No evidence of network segmentation, private subnets, or least-privilege security groups.
findings.recommendation: Define VPC with private subnets for database, security groups with least-privilege rules, ALB in public subnets.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: Application served directly by Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi. No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront.
findings.gap: Services exposed directly with no gateway or load balancer — no throttling, no request validation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy ALB as entry point with health checks. Consider API Gateway for throttling and auth.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Single statically-provisioned EC2 instance. All capacity is fixed.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — all capacity statically provisioned. Cannot respond to traffic changes.
findings.recommendation: After containerization, configure ECS service auto-scaling with target-tracking policies.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: Only backup is daily pg_dump cron mentioned in README. No PITR, no retention policy, no tested restore.
findings.gap: Minimal backup with no PITR, no defined retention, no tested restore. Up to 24-hour data loss window.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS for automated backups with PITR. Implement AWS Backup with defined retention.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: Zero infrastructure defined as code. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or any IaC tool present.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage — all infrastructure created manually. No reproducibility or audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Adopt AWS CDK or Terraform. Start with VPC, subnets, security groups, compute, and database.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Deployment is manual git pull + Apache restart per README.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments manual. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.recommendation: Implement AWS CodePipeline with CodeBuild. Stages: lint/SAST → test → build → deploy to staging → production.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Python 2.7 (EOL Jan 2020) with Django 1.4 (EOL Oct 2015). Both language and framework are end-of-life. No AWS SDK.
findings.gap: Compound legacy — language (Python 2.7 EOL), framework (Django 1.4 EOL), and no AWS SDK all regressed.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Python 3.12+ with Django 5.x or FastAPI. Enables modern AWS SDK (boto3) and cloud-native ecosystem.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries. 2 source files, raw SQL in views, no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: No module boundaries, pervasive shared state, no architectural patterns. Cannot scale independently.
findings.recommendation: Introduce Django models, service layer, repository pattern. Foundation for future Strangler Fig extraction.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication synchronous. Synchronous DB queries and SMTP within request processing. No async patterns for a stateful-crud service.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous HTTP with no async patterns. Email notifications block response.
findings.recommendation: Introduce asynchronous messaging (SQS/EventBridge) for state-change propagation and email decoupling.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No background job processing for a stateful-crud service.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous — no async job processing pattern for bulk operations or reports.
findings.recommendation: Implement background jobs with SQS + Lambda/ECS workers for operations exceeding 30 seconds.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning. No /v1/ paths, no version headers, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly with no backward compatibility.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (/v1/tickets/) with N-1 version support policy.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All endpoints hardcoded: DB at 127.0.0.1:5432, email at exchange.internal.corp:25. No dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hard-coded — no dynamic discovery, no environment-based configuration.
findings.recommendation: Externalize endpoints to environment variables or AWS SSM Parameter Store. Adopt Cloud Map for multi-service.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: No managed object storage. Static files on local disk. Any attachments on local EC2 filesystem. No S3.
findings.gap: Data on local file systems with no managed storage, no accessibility, no durability guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon S3 for static files and document storage. Add lifecycle policies and Textract for search.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Raw SQL queries scattered in view functions. No repository/DAO pattern, no ORM despite Django providing one.
findings.gap: Database queries scattered with no pattern — raw SQL embedded in HTTP handlers.
findings.recommendation: Implement Django models (ORM) or repository pattern. Centralizes access, eliminates SQL injection.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 (EOL November 2016). Over 9 years without security patches. 10+ major versions behind current.
findings.gap: Database engine past EOL. No version pinning in IaC. Critical security and performance fixes unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS PostgreSQL latest (16.x). Test with pg_upgrade or DMS. Major version gap may require app updates.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Self-managed PostgreSQL on EC2 with no disk encryption, no KMS. Data stored in plaintext.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest configured. Sensitive helpdesk data stored in plaintext on unencrypted storage.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS for automatic encryption. Configure customer-managed KMS keys with rotation.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: No authentication. Views have no auth decorators, no auth middleware in MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES. Endpoints completely open.
findings.gap: No API authentication — endpoints open. Any user can access ticket data without credentials.
findings.recommendation: Implement authentication with Amazon Cognito for OAuth2/JWT. Add @login_required to all views.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. No Cognito, OIDC, SAML, or SSO. Application has no authentication at all.
findings.gap: No authentication system — neither standalone nor centralized. No external IdP.
findings.recommendation: Implement Amazon Cognito as IdP with SSO to corporate identity provider.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in settings.py: SECRET_KEY and database PASSWORD committed to version control.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code. Critical security vulnerability — exposed to all with repo access.
findings.recommendation: Rotate credentials immediately. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Scrub git history.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy. Ubuntu 12.04 (EOL), Apache 2.2 (EOL). No vulnerability scanning of any kind.
findings.gap: Running EOL OS and web server. No patching automation, no vulnerability scanning.
findings.recommendation: Use hardened base images (Bottlerocket for ECS). Implement ECR scanning and AWS Inspector.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning. Known SQL injection/XSS vulnerabilities undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools — known vulnerabilities exist undetected in the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (CodeGuru/Semgrep) and pip-audit in CI/CD pipeline as blocking gates.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry. Only debug print statements.
findings.gap: No tracing — no request flow visibility or cross-service correlation.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with AWS X-Ray SDK or OpenTelemetry (ADOT) for distributed tracing.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring, no service level targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for ticket listing (p99 < 500ms, availability > 99.5%). Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics. No business metrics (tickets created/resolved, resolution time). No dashboards.
findings.gap: No custom metrics — no business outcome tracking.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics to CloudWatch: tickets_created, mean_resolution_time. Create dashboards.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no PagerDuty. Failures detected only by user complaints.
findings.gap: No alerting — system failures undetected until user reports.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on error rates and p99 latency. Integrate with PagerDuty/OpsGenie.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. No unit tests, no integration tests, no test configuration. Zero coverage.
findings.gap: No tests — any code change carries full regression risk with no safety net.
findings.recommendation: Implement pytest with Django test client. Start with integration tests for critical paths. Add >80% coverage gate.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no alarms with owners, no team attribution.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring non-existent and reactive.
findings.recommendation: Establish CODEOWNERS for observability configs, named alarm owners, per-service dashboards.
